cars.variant: Racing Puma — original UK road specification
cars.specification_market: Stephen Dobie’s actual driving report dated 17 December 2016 supplies road-model evidence and expressly distinguishes the Racing Puma from rally cars. Retain its native quoted 153 bhp, not prototype ST160 targets, the later Puma SUV or independently tuned examples. Optional limited-slip differential, proposed replacement dampers, unverified stopping-force claim, exact track dimensions and press-car-specific spacers are excluded. No extra standard Puma or cosmetic edition is counted.
cars.summary: The Racing Puma is a lasting compact fast-Ford icon whose wide-track chassis, Alcon brakes and Tickford conversion gave the small coupe a distinctive driving identity. Its significance lies in the road car’s handling and enthusiast following, rather than a race result, rarity or power figure alone.

cars.generation: Original DB2 production-road sporting coupe family
cars.variant: DB2 Vantage — documented 1952 LML/50/102 road-car reference
cars.specification_market: RM’s inspection/history-file catalogue identifies 1952 chassis LML/50/102 and engine VB6B/50/553. Its Heritage Trust certificate and factory service card record Vantage uprating before US delivery. Select this restored production customer coupe; no prototype, Le Mans Lightweight, DB2/4 or unique Graber body is substituted. The car was later converted to right-hand drive and its engine rebuilt in 2005, so current originality and measured output are not certified. No universal horsepower figure is inferred.
cars.summary: The DB2 established the postwar David Brown Aston Martin sporting lineage, bringing Lagonda-derived twin-cam six-cylinder engineering to an influential road GT. The documented customer coupe adds a foundational performance-car family before the DB4 and DB5, rather than an experimental car or a coachwork variation.
